source/references/durrett-probability-2019-01-11/PTE5_011119.pdf PDF p. 49 = printed p. 41: Example 1.7.8 (axiom of choice and continuum hypothesis order) and its lead-in on measurability and set-theoretic axioms
components.note: All four source examples are stated with their exact data and values and proved at annex 393-493: (1) power-set product, counting product, section sums 1/0 and 0, infinite f+ and f- integrals; (2) section integrals (e^-x - e^-2x)/x in (0,1] and (e^-2y - e^-y)/y with absolute value <= e^-y, strict signs, and divergence of both part integrals from explicit lower bounds c+/x, c-/(4x) and the dyadic divergence of integral dx/x, via Tonelli; (3) counting measure on an uncountable set is a measure but not sigma-finite, the diagonal is product measurable by rational rectangles, iterated values 1 and 0, no common product value; (4) under the explicit premise of a bijection b: omega_1 -> (0,1) (the form of AC+CH used), countable initial segments give section integrals 0 and 1, and Tonelli for probability factors gives non-measurability; conditionality is retained. Durrett's lead-ins (hypotheses needed, sigma-finiteness needed, measurability matters and the set-theoretic premise) are reflected in the item causes, item 4's conditional statement and the warning def:p15-product-completion-domain. Observation, not a gap: item 2's product measurability is justified by continuity and the Borel-product theorem (annex 409-410); it also follows at once from measurable coordinates (thm:p15-product-sections) and thm:p15-measurable-operations.
